bull.t: Broad organic growth and margin expansion
bull.b: Broad growth across regions and segments, combined with expanding gross and operating margins, indicates durable demand and operating leverage. This supports continued earnings growth if procedure volumes and hospital spending remain healthy.

bull.t: Strong free cash flow and improving leverage
bull.b: High free-cash-flow conversion provides funding for innovation, acquisitions, debt reduction and shareholder returns. Deleveraging from prior periods also improves financial flexibility and reduces balance-sheet risk over the medium term.

A steady cadence of product launches and rising Mako utilization strengthens Stryker’s technology offering and supports procedure-based recurring demand. AVS adds intravascular lithotripsy capability, broadening future growth opportunities.

bear.b: The disruption exposes execution and supply-chain concentration risk in a growth category, with lost sales and backorders affecting results. Although management expects improvement by the end of Q3, recovery depends on restoring reliable production.

Residual cybersecurity costs can weigh on earnings and cash generation beyond the initial disruption while management allocates resources to remediation. Continued spending also indicates operational resilience and infrastructure remain areas of risk.

bear.t: Meaningful debt and uneven cash conversion
bear.b: Leverage has improved, but sizable absolute debt limits flexibility if acquisition activity or financing costs rise. Operating cash flow below EBITDA also shows that working capital and cash-cost timing can periodically weaken the quality of earnings conversion.
